briefs.C1-C3:
Every Phase 2 slice (S1 to S12) is merged on post-emudhra-phase2 (25b222e), and the full check list passes there. This run is not a §10.2 slice. The owner read review/phase2_code_notes.md on 2026-10-31 and said "fix C1 to C6 first". Your scope is the code notes named below, and nothing else: read each one in full in review/phase2_code_notes.md (its note, suggestion and Checked line), then the spec sections it cites. Where these instructions say "the slice's file list", they mean the files listed here.
Two runs go side by side: C1 to C3 (the wallet, ui/, plus one exported node constant) and C4 to C6 (ledger/genesis.go, node/persist.go, signing/scheme.go). Stay in your files so the merge is clean.
Commit each note separately with the subject "phase 2 C<n>: <what>". Do not edit review/: the orchestrator updates the spec, the code notes and the progress note after the merge.
If a change makes a sentence in the docs false, fix that sentence in the same commit: ui/README.md, ui/USER_MANUAL.md, docs/*.md (including docs/reading-the-code.md) and README.md. Change only the lines about your change, so the other run's doc edits merge cleanly. Do not touch findings.md or findings_20261027.md: they are dated records.
The owner wants the smallest change that does the job.

Your notes are C1, C2 and C3.
- C1 (ui/trust.go signedByPinned, plus ui/trust_test.go). Take option (a): keep only the votes of pinned names that verify under their pinned key, then call Commit.Verify. That restores the rule spec §7.2 and Q17 state: the pin fails only once a third or more of the pinned power has left or re-keyed. The test must cover a pinned name that signs under a new key, both with the other pinned names above ⅔ (verifies) and below it (does not). Check that trust.go's top comment, ui/README.md and the guide's step 20 are then true as written.
- C2 (ui/wallet.go ReviewPayment and UpdateAccount, plus tests). Before the wallet takes a counter block, it runs the ledger's own checks against the verified state: ledger.PaymentFitsState and ledger.CreditFitsBalanceCap for a payment (in ReviewPayment, so the review page shows the reason), and ledger.UpdateFitsState for an update (before nextPaymentBlockID). Keep the existing friendly messages where they are clearer, but the ledger's rule must decide. Remember that a refused review or update must not use up a counter block: test that too. The S10 note in ui/USER_MANUAL.md and ui/README.md about the payment counter ("wait for the chain to advance") may describe which refusals use a block; keep it true.
- C3 (ui/wallet.go LoadOrCreateWallet, ui/main.go's -lookahead flag help, ui/README.md, the -lookahead sentence in docs/operating-a-network.md around 'raise the wallet's -lookahead'). Export the node's window as node.MaxBlockIDLookahead (rename maxBlockIDLookahead in node/ and its tests; touch nothing else in node/). LoadOrCreateWallet refuses a lookahead above node.MaxBlockIDLookahead - blockSlack (32 today), with an error that names the node's 64-block window. A value below 1 keeps today's default of 3. Say the ceiling in the flag's help and in ui/README.md's flag table. Update docs/reading-the-code.md where it names maxBlockIDLookahead.

Your notes are C4, C5 and C6.
- C4 (ledger/genesis.go ValidateGenesis, plus its tests). Refuse a static validator's power above consensus.MaxValidatorPower (2^40), next to the 'Power < 1' check, with a message that names the field and the bound, as the function's other refusals do. Do not change NewValidatorSet's saturation: dynamic mode relies on it. If docs/operating-a-network.md (or another doc) states the allowed power range of a genesis validator, give the ceiling there.
- C5 (node/persist.go writeAtomic, plus a test in node/). When writeAtomic fails after it has created the temporary file, remove the temporary file. Write it in the plainest form for a reader who is not a Go expert. Add no logging (the note's 'optionally log' is not taken). The test must fail without the change: for example, make the rename fail and check that no temporary file is left.
- C6 (signing/scheme.go: the package comment and Scheme's comment). Make the claim exact, as the note suggests: Signer has no method that signs raw bytes, and every check rebuilds the domain preimage. PrivateKey.Sign takes raw bytes, and only Signer and test keys call it. A Scheme does not sign at all; its PrivateKey does. Keep the audit C1 context in one sentence. Comments only. report.summary:
C1 to C3 are fixed on p2-c1c3, one commit per note, in worktree <scratch>/wt/p2-c1c3.

C1 (ui/trust.go signedByPinned): option (a), a one-line change. It keeps a pinned name's vote only when the vote verifies under that name's pinned key, then calls Commit.Verify. One re-keyed pinned bank no longer stops verification. The pin fails only once a third or more of the pinned power has left or re-keyed (spec 7.2, Q17). trust.go's top comment, ui/README.md's pin paragraph and the guide's step 20 are now true as written. Only signedByPinned's own comment changed, plus the step 20 test count (16 to 17).

C2 (ui/wallet.go):
- ReviewPayment now runs ledger.PaymentFitsState and ledger.CreditFitsBalanceCap against the verified state, so the review page shows the ledger's reason. Send still takes its counter block only after ReviewPayment.
- UpdateAccount runs ledger.UpdateFitsState before nextPaymentBlockID.
- The hand-written payee check is gone. The ledger's messages are clearer: they name the payee and say whether it has no account or is frozen.
- The "amount must be positive" and "nothing to update" messages stay.
- Docs: ui/README.md "Known behaviour" and the ui/USER_MANUAL.md FAQ now say that only a refusal by the node uses up a block, so the stall comes after 33 refusals by the node. In the guide, step 21's "checks the network's own rules first" bullet names the new checks, its test run now counts 38, and step 23 hop 1 shows the calls.

C3:
- The constant is renamed maxBlockIDLookahead to node.MaxBlockIDLookahead across node/ and its tests, comments included. Nothing else in node/ changed.
- LoadOrCreateWallet refuses a lookahead above node.MaxBlockIDLookahead - blockSlack (32). The error names the node's 64-block window. A value below 1 is still 3.
- The -lookahead flag's help gives the ceiling, computed from the constants. So do ui/README.md's flag table and the sentence in docs/operating-a-network.md (its paragraph is rewrapped). The guide names MaxBlockIDLookahead.

The case with two pinned plus the re-keyed one does not verify, before or after the fix.

report.openIssues:
- The disk is full. / has about 74 MB free (90 of 94 GB used, 13 GB of it in ~/.cache/go-build). A last per-commit scratch build ran out of space. I deleted only my own scratch copies under p2-scratch (c1-revert, c2-revert, c2-late, c3-revert, c1c3-commits, wallet-bin) and nothing else. The parallel C4–C6 run, and any merge or check run, may hit 'no space left on device' until the owner frees space, for example by running go clean -cache.
- Size-check gap in C2 (wallet side): the wallet runs PaymentFitsState and UpdateFitsState on the unsigned message, so their WithinMessageBound check misses the 4,412-character signature. An update whose description and address together are about 1,900 to 6,300 bytes passes the wallet's check, the node refuses it, and it uses a block. Payments are not affected at default parameters, since the wallet sends no comment. Closing this needs a size check that counts the signature. That is more than the smallest change, so I left it.
- The node can still refuse for reasons the wallet cannot see: the overdraw guard counting pooled payments, a fee of the payer's in that block (409), a node state newer than the wallet's, or a full pool. Those still use up a block, and the docs now say that only refusals by the node do.
- The USER_MANUAL FAQ 'The node refused my payment' still lists below the fee, above the largest payment and a name that cannot be paid. These can still happen when the state changes between review and send, but the review now catches them first. I left it unchanged, since it is not false.

problems.problem: UpdateAccount runs ledger.UpdateFitsState on the unsigned update, which has no BlockID and an empty Signature. That check includes WithinMessageBound, so it does not count the 4,412-character signature. At the default MaxMessageBytes of 6400, an update whose description and address together are about 1,900 to 6,300 bytes passes the wallet's check. The wallet then takes a counter block and sends the update, and every node refuses it as 'update too large'. This makes two new sentences false for that case: the UpdateAccount comment ('so an update that could not apply uses up no block') and ui/README.md 'Known behaviour' ('one that fails them uses no block'). The wallet form puts no length limit on the description. Payments are not affected: the wallet sends no comment, and MinMessageBytes always fits the largest signed payment. The builder reported this gap under openIssues.
problems.evidence: In a scratch test (kept at <scratch>/p2-scratch/verify-C1-C3-logs/zz_verify_test.go), UpdateAccount with a 3,000-byte description returns err=nil and blockID=13, and one post is sent. ledger.UpdateFitsState on the posted signed update, against default parameters, returns 'update too large: its serialized form exceeds the governed message bound'. The next UpdateAccount names block 14, so the refused update used up block 13.
problems.fix: Run the check on a copy that has the signed size. For example: measured := update; measured.BlockID, measured.Signature = math.MaxInt64, strings.Repeat("A", base64.StdEncoding.EncodedLen(mldsa.MLDSA65SignatureSize)), then UpdateFitsState(checkpoint.State, measured). That is about 2 lines. The other option is to leave the code as it is and narrow the comment and the README sentence so they do not cover a size refusal.

verdict.evidence:
I checked the C1 to C3 slice on p2-c1c3 (HEAD dea5136) against the code notes C1 to C3, spec §0, §7.2, §7.3 and Q17, and the computed task. The slice is correct and complete, apart from one minor problem.

**C1 (ui/trust.go signedByPinned).** It is option (a). The filter keeps a pinned name's vote only when vote.Verify passes under pinned.PublicKey(vote.Validator), then calls Commit.Verify.
- It is safe: only valid votes under pinned keys count, and duplicates and mismatched heights, rounds or blocks are still refused by Commit.Verify. The only thing it relaxes is the re-keyed or invalid votes, which are now left out.
- The first-use path is unchanged.
- Three docs are now true as written: trust.go's top comment, ui/README.md's pin paragraph (line 53) and the guide's step 20.
- Reverting trust.go to 25b222e in a scratch copy fails TestPinnedQuorumLeavesOutARekeyedPinnedName with 'case 0: got false, want true'.

**C2 (ui/wallet.go).**
- ReviewPayment runs ledger.PaymentFitsState and ledger.CreditFitsBalanceCap after registeredName.
- Send still takes its block only after ReviewPayment.
- UpdateAccount runs ledger.UpdateFitsState before nextPaymentBlockID.
- Reverting wallet.go to d46ce5c fails both new tests: 5 and 3 requests are sent, and every refusal is missing.
- Two mutations also fail: Send taking the block before ReviewPayment ('names block 18, want 13'), and the update check moved after nextPaymentBlockID ('names block 16, want 13').
- Disabling only CreditFitsBalanceCap fails the 'full' case.
- The docs (README 'Known behaviour', the USER_MANUAL FAQ, the guide's step 21 and step 23 hop 1) are accurate, apart from the size case above.

**C3.**
- maxBlockIDLookahead is renamed to MaxBlockIDLookahead in node/. The diff in node/ touches only that identifier: 29 lines across mempool.go, node.go, requestpool.go, updatepool.go and five test files. No old name is left anywhere outside review/.
- LoadOrCreateWallet sets a lookahead below 1 to 3. It refuses one above node.MaxBlockIDLookahead - blockSlack (32), with an error naming 'the node's 64-block window', before any key file is created or any passphrase is asked for.

**Not a problem.** node/mempool.go's comment says the 64 'is slack for a node that is behind'. At the largest lookahead a wallet burst now uses all 64. That was already so before this slice, and the task forbids other edits in node/.

fixed: ui/wallet.go UpdateAccount (minor; signature not counted in the size check), commit d227efa 'phase 2 C1-C3: the wallet measures an update as signed before it takes a block (review follow-up)'. The wallet now runs ledger.UpdateFitsState on a copy of the update that has a signature's length (strings.Repeat("A", base64.StdEncoding.EncodedLen(mldsa.MLDSA65SignatureSize)), 4,412 characters) and the widest block number (math.MaxInt64). The node measures the signed update the same way, so an update too large to send is refused before nextPaymentBlockID takes a block. The block number is overcounted by at most about 18 bytes; the comment says so. It is a 3-line change plus the 'math' import. The UpdateAccount doc comment now says the size is 'measured as signed'. With the fix, that comment and the ui/README.md 'Known behaviour' sentence ('one that fails them uses no block') are true as written, so the README is unchanged. Payments are left as they are: the wallet sends no comment, and MinMessageBytes (5000) fits the largest signed payment.

Test: TestAccountUpdateRunsTheLedgersRules (ui/wallet_test.go) now also refuses a 3,000-byte description with 'update too large'. Under the default MaxMessageBytes of 6400, that description fits only until the signature is added. The test still checks that nothing was posted and that the next update names block 13. Without the fix (HEAD dea5136's wallet.go plus the new test, in a scratch copy) it fails: 'want a refusal saying "update too large"' is reported with err <nil>, then '1 request(s) sent for updates the ledger refuses'. The test's error message now prints the description's length instead of quoting it, so a failure does not dump 3,000 characters. No new test was added, so the test counts in the guide's step 21 stay the same.

commits.subject: phase 2 C4: the genesis refuses a static validator's power above 2^40
phase 2 C5: writeAtomic removes its temporary file when the write fails

report.summary:
C4, C5 and C6 are fixed on branch p2-c4c6 in worktree <scratch>/wt/p2-c4c6, one commit each, on top of 25b222e. 7 files changed: 55 lines added, 15 removed.

C4 (<scratch>/wt/p2-c4c6/ledger/genesis.go): ValidateGenesis now refuses a static validator whose power is above consensus.MaxValidatorPower. The check sits next to the 'Power < 1' check. The message names the field and the bound: `validators: the power of "bank-b" is 1099511627777, above 1099511627776 (2^40, consensus.MaxValidatorPower)`. The file gains an import of consensus. NewValidatorSet's saturation is not changed. docs/operating-a-network.md, in the paragraph that lists the refusals, now says "power below 1 or above 2^40 (`consensus.MaxValidatorPower`)".

C5 (<scratch>/wt/p2-c4c6/node/persist.go): writeAtomic can fail at four steps after it has created the temporary file: Write, Sync, Close and Rename. Each of those error paths now calls os.Remove(temporaryPath) before it returns. That is four plain lines and no defer. No logging is added. The doc comment says why: the backup mirror names a new temporary file at each height. A failure after the rename (opening or syncing the folder) has nothing to remove, since the file has already become the target.

C6 (<scratch>/wt/p2-c4c6/signing/scheme.go): comments only.
- The package comment keeps the audit C1 context in one sentence. It then says what holds: Signer, the type all production code signs with, has no method that signs raw bytes; it signs only a length-prefixed preimage that binds a Domain and the network id; and every check (Verify, VerifyBase64) rebuilds that preimage. PrivateKey.Sign does take raw bytes, and outside tests only Signer.Sign calls it.
- Scheme's comment now says that a Scheme does not sign; the PrivateKey it parses does.
- I checked the claim with grep over non-test code. PrivateKey.Sign is called only in signer.go. crypto/mldsa signs only in mldsa65.go. Scheme.Verify is called only by signing.Verify. cmd/server's key self-test goes through Signer.Sign with a Domain.

tests.name: ledger TestGenesisRefusesWhatNoLedgerCouldHold, new case 'a validator above the power cap' (power 2^40 + 1)
tests.failsWithoutChange: Yes. In a scratch copy at 25b222e with only the new test file, it fails with: ValidateGenesis accepted a genesis it must refuse (want an error mentioning "the power of \"bank-b\" is 1099511627777, above 1099511627776 ..."). It passes with the change. The same test also checks that a power of exactly 2^40 is still accepted. That check guards against an off-by-one and passes either way.

tests.name: node TestFailedWriteLeavesNoTemporaryFile (node/persist_test.go)
tests.failsWithoutChange: Yes. The test puts a folder where the file should go, so the rename fails. In a scratch copy at 35f0589 (before C5) with only the new test file, it fails with: the failed write left its temporary file .../backup.json.7.tmp behind (<nil>). It passes with the change.

problems.problem: writeAtomic's new doc sentence says "A write that fails before its rename removes its temp file". The code also removes the file when the rename itself fails, and that is the exact path the new test covers. A reader who is not a Go expert could take the sentence to mean that a failed rename leaves the file behind.
problems.evidence: node/persist.go lines 114-116 of the comment say "fails before its rename". The body has `if err := os.Rename(temporaryPath, path); err != nil { os.Remove(temporaryPath); return err }`. TestFailedWriteLeavesNoTemporaryFile makes exactly the rename fail.

verdict.evidence:
I reviewed branch p2-c4c6 (HEAD d1df5dd, three commits on 25b222e) against review/phase2_code_notes.md C4 to C6, spec §2.2 and the orchestrator's instructions. The worktree is clean, review/ is not touched, and only the expected 7 files changed. Each commit subject is "phase 2 C<n>: ...", with an evidence body and the Co-Authored-By trailer.

C4 (ledger/genesis.go):
- The ceiling check sits right after the `Power < 1` check. Its message names the field and the bound, like the function's other refusals.
- NewValidatorSet's saturation is unchanged.
- StaticValidators are filled only in ValidateGenesis (checked with grep), so the check covers every static path.
- docs/operating-a-network.md now gives "below 1 or above 2^40". No other doc states the genesis power range: architecture.md, consensus.md, security.md and reading-the-code.md speak only of saturation, which is still true.
- Revert test: in a scratch copy with genesis.go restored to 25b222e, TestGenesisRefusesWhatNoLedgerCouldHold/a_validator_above_the_power_cap FAILS ("ValidateGenesis accepted a genesis it must refuse"). It passes at HEAD.
- Adversarial: powers 2^40+1, 3*2^40 and MaxInt64 are all refused with the named message. Every seat at exactly 2^40 is accepted, and the set's total equals N*2^40.

C5 (node/persist.go):
- Each of the four failure paths after OpenFile (Write, Sync, Close, Rename) calls os.Remove(temporaryPath). There is no defer and no logging.
- A failure after the rename has nothing to remove.
- The sign log and the snapshot are written only on the loop, so a Remove cannot race another writer of the same temporary path.
- Revert test: in a scratch copy with persist.go restored to 25b222e, TestFailedWriteLeavesNoTemporaryFile FAILS ("left its temporary file ... backup.json.7.tmp behind"). It passes at HEAD.
- Adversarial tests of my own pass at HEAD:
  - The temporary path is a symlink to /dev/full, so Write fails with ENOSPC. The symlink is removed, /dev/full is untouched and no target is created.
  - A rename over a non-empty folder fails and keeps the folder's contents, and only the target is left in the directory.
  - A successful write leaves only the target.
- I ran TestHungBackupMountHoldsOneMirror (FIFOs; the mirror goroutine now removes the FIFO during cleanup), TestBackupMirrorsSnapshot, TestSoleValidatorRestart* and the new test under -race -count=6: ok.
- The guide's step 14 pattern lists 25 tests with go test -list, and it covers every Test in persist_test, restart_test, backup_test and backup_unix_test.

C6 (signing/scheme.go, comments only):
- I checked the claims with grep over non-test code in both modules:
  - PrivateKey.Sign is called only at signer.go:44.
  - Scheme.Verify is called only by signing.Verify.
  - All production signing goes through signing.Signer: ledger, consensus, cmd/server, cmd/demo and ui/wallet.go.
  - ui/keyfile.go calls ParsePrivateKey only to derive the public key.
  - Preimage is in domain.go, as the comment says.
- The audit C1 context is one sentence. Scheme's comment now says a Scheme does not sign and its PrivateKey does.
- README.md:100, docs/security.md:30 and docs/signature.md:44-46 say "the only signing API the node and the wallet use", which is accurate for production. signing_test.go:226 calls privateKey.Sign directly, but that is test code.

Suite at d1df5dd, run myself with GOTOOLCHAIN=auto (go1.27.3):
- gofmt -l . gives no output; go vet ./... and go vet -C ui ./... are clean; go build ./... and go build -C ui -o /dev/null . succeed.
- GOLEDGER_CHAOS_SLACK=4 go test -race -count=1 ./... passed twice:
  - run 1: consensus 55.4s, ledger 13.8s, node 66.5s, signing, cmd/demo and cmd/server ok;
  - run 2: consensus 54.5s, node 67.4s, all ok.
- The same with -C ui passed twice (35.0s / 34.8s).
- -race -count=3 -run 'Chaos|Restart|SignLog|Resume|CatchUp' ./node/ passed (89.3s).

Environment note, not a code problem: the / volume that holds /tmp/claude-<uid> filled up during this run (the parallel C1-C3 run was also running tests). My first suite attempt failed to link node.test with "no space left on device", so I stopped it. I reran the suite with GOCACHE, GOTMPDIR and TMPDIR pointed at a folder of my own in /dev/shm (tmpfs, 32G free). I removed that folder and my scratch copies (verify-C4-C6-1 to -4) afterwards. I deleted nothing else. The orchestrator should know that / is at 100% (the Go build cache in ~/.cache/go-build is 13G).

The one minor point (the wording of writeAtomic's comment) does not block the merge. There is no blocker or major problem.
